title: Many bad inputs force distributional error
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $p$ be a deterministic one-way protocol for the Index function on $n$-bit strings and indices in $[n]$, with Boolean output. Call a string bad if no answer vector produced by any message of $p$ lies at Hamming distance less than $n/4$ from it. If at least $2^{n-1}$ strings are bad, then the probability that $p$ errs on a uniformly chosen pair consisting of an $n$-bit string and an index in $[n]$ is at least $1/8$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic one-way protocol with finite nonempty message set and Boolean output
At least $2^{n-1}$ of Alice's $n$-bit strings have no protocol answer vector at Hamming distance less than $n/4$
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic one-way protocol for $\mathrm{IND}_n$.  If at least $2^{n-1}$ of
Alice's $2^n$ inputs are bad for $p$ (no answer vector of $p$ lies within Hamming distance
$n/4$), then the distributional error of $p$ on $\mathrm{IND}_n$ under the uniform
distribution on pairs $(x, i)$ is at least $1/8$.
